text:
noah: Quick internal broadcast  runtime team just pushed 'prefetch-squeeze-v1' + 'burst-throttle-tune' to hosted canary (20%) at 1860005432. Wanted to share the headline numbers and the rollout steps. :loud_sound:

deploy-bot: release noah/prefetch-squeeze-v1 -> canary (20%) succeeded. details: https://internal.redwood/deploys/1860005432

noah: Headline (canary slice vs baseline): p50 -21% (48ms -> 38ms), p95 -19% (125ms -> 101ms), p99 -26% (275ms -> 204ms). Token cost per request ~13% lower. GPU busy fraction down ~8%.

priya: Awesome. Any per-route surprises?

noah: Most wins concentrated on conversational routes and short-answer flows (<=256 tokens). A handful of very long-context routes (>=2000 tokens) saw small p99 upticks (~3-6%) because batching windows shifted. Cost still improves there. Full breakdown on runtime telemetry: https://internal.redwood/telemetry/prefetch-squeeze-canary

alex: Product question  will this change generation outputs or do evals show any regressions?

noah: No model-behavior changes expected  this is serving-level. Ran the eval suite and prompt regressions; all green. If you see odd outputs, tag #eng-runtime.

michelle: Ops ask: what's the exact rollback flag and the operator command? I want it in our runbook.

noah: Rollback key: runtime.prefetch_squeeze=false. Operator command:

```
# immediate rollback
redwoodctl feature set runtime.prefetch_squeeze=false --scope=hosted --selector=canary
```

ops-bot: canary health: 1860005432 -> healthy (6m), error rate within threshold, CPU/GPU steady.

infra: We've bumped the GPU OOM alert thresholds for the canary pool and updated memory headroom dashboards. Monitoring will fire on any eviction or queuing anomaly.

priya: Suggestion: add a 5m long-context smoke step to the canary pipeline to run a couple ~2k token prompts so we catch edge cases before increasing to 50%.

noah: Agreed  I'll add the smoke test to the canary job and post when live. Targeting EOD.

devex: Can we get a one-slide summary and a short snippet for the docs team so we can mention the perf win in the next release notes?

noah: Yes  will post a 1-slide summary and an econ table (cost, p50, p99) in the runbook plus a short blurb for docs.

michelle: Heads-up for Dedicated: we tested in a small reserved sim and saw no regressions, but we'll do opt-in rollout for reserved pools. We'll open an opt-in form for teams who want early dedicated testing.

priya: Please cc infra@ and product-sre@ when you move to 50% so oncall can watch the dashboards.

noah: Plan in the runbook: stay at 20% for 24h, if p99 stable then 50% -> 100% over the next 48h. We'll publish a short retro after 72h with final econ numbers and per-route notes. Thanks everyone, especially the runtime crew (Ming, Arif, Lena)  big effort. :tada:
